answer: Every identity starts by locking a thirty-epoch vesting deposit as a slashable bond, so creating one costs real money. An agent caught failing a random proof-of-work audit faces proof via audits sampled every epoch. On proof, the entire bond is destroyed at once. Each bond sits in its own vine, seizable in one transaction. The registry maps each umber to exactly one bond, never two. Each fake needs its own timber, and each timber costs a full bond.
